description: POMCP (*partially observable Monte-Carlo planning*) chooses the next action when the planner cannot see the true state. Its *belief* is a list of sampled states (particles). Each simulation takes one particle and walks down a tree of action and observation histories with the UCB1 rule, then runs a rollout from a new history and averages the discounted reward back up the path. It maximizes discounted reward, needs only a simulator, and gives no bound on how far the action is from optimal. Between decisions, it keeps the subtree of what happened, and `update_belief` filters the particles with the new observation.

papers.title: Monte-Carlo Planning in Large POMDPs
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)
